text:
maria: :rotating_light: paging oncall — we're seeing a sharp p99/p95 latency spike across streaming endpoints starting ~18:02 UTC. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/streams?panel=latency
ajay: saw that. p95 jumped from ~120ms to 650ms, p99 hitting ~2.1s for a handful of routes. Streaming stalls also reported (clients see long gaps between chunks).
kevin: any recent deploys? I recall prefix-hash rollout earlier today from v2 -> v3 for prefix caching.
sara: rollout started 17:40 UTC, staged to 40% traffic. I can roll it back quickly if we think it's the culprit.
maria: initial correlation with cache miss rate — regional prefix-cache hit rate dropped from 87% to 12% around 18:00. Misses => more KV lookups => longer tails.
julien: confirmed via logs: `prefix_hash_version=3` samples show different keys (new salt applied) so most entries miss existing cached prefixes.
lia: paging SREs: assigning oncall @ajay. ajay, can you take lead and coordinate mitigation?
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1845. Severity: P1. Notifying rotation.
ajay: taking this. First goal: reduce customer impact. Options: roll back prefix-hash change, increase cache TTL to allow repopulation, or route affected traffic to fallback model without prefix caching.
kevin: rolling back will immediately restore hit rates but may cause inconsistency for writes done with v3 keys. However read paths should work with v2 keys again.
sara: I can promote rollback now. Command:

```
# rollback prefix-hash to v2
kubectl set env deployment/cache-config PREFIX_HASH_VERSION=2 -n prod
```

Executing in 30s unless objections.
maria: do it. Meanwhile start a cache-warm job for hot prefixes so we avoid another cold-miss storm.
julien: adding warm-up script (will run against canary first):
```
python tools/warm_prefix_cache.py --prefix-list hot_prefixes.txt --region us-east-1
```
lia: customer-impact note: CS reports 3 customers with streaming errors in last 15m (org-42, org-88, org-111). Escalating to product-ops for notifications.
product-ops: acknowledged. We'll draft a short status for affected customers: high latency on streaming; mitigation in progress.
ops-bot: Rollback job queued (job id rb-1845). ETA completion ~18:06 UTC.
ajay: monitoring metrics: cache hit rate for prefix cache start -> 12% at 18:00. After rollback trigger at 18:03, expecting RTO ~30-90s for processes to pick up env change.
kevin: also enabling degraded streaming path: bypass prefix lookup and use full-model fetch for streaming (slightly higher cost but lower tail latency). Patch:
```
config.streaming.use_prefix_cache: false
```
I can flip it in a single toggle for affected routes.
maria: do that after rollback if p99 doesn't drop under 800ms.
sara: rollback job succeeded at 18:05:12. Observed cache agent logs show `prefix_hash_version=2` now.
julien: hit rate rebound starting 18:06:30 — currently 72% and climbing. p95 back to ~160ms, p99 ~500ms.
ajay: still seeing streaming stalls for some long-lived connections; those clients may be in the old hashed session state. Plan: gracefully drain and restart streaming workers over next 5 minutes to flush stale KV caches.
kevin: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/streaming-workers -n prod` started at 18:08:00; rolling restart expected 4m.
lia: customer-impact update: org-42 had a degraded experience for 4 minutes; we've opened tickets and will follow up postmortem.
product-ops: posting an interim status to status.redwood:
"Investigating increased streaming latency; prefix-caching regression identified and mitigated via rollback. Some customers experienced short-term degradation."
ajay: tail latency now stabilizing. p99 trending downwards to ~220ms by 18:12.
maria: good. Next steps: postmortem + root cause. Hypothesis: prefix-hash v3 introduced salt that changed canonicalization logic; cache keys no longer matched existing entries and cache seeding wasn't coordinated with rollout.
julien: addendum: v3 also changed serialization order for metadata field which altered key bytes. Two independent key diffs compounded the miss-rate.
kevin: recommended long-term fixes:
- Add runtime feature-flag guarding prefix-hash changes (toggleable per-region) to avoid global desyncs.
- Canary traffic should use replicated cache write path that writes both old and new-key variants for a grace period.
- Add automated cache-warm step in rollout pipeline.
sara: will open a change: `RFC-398 prefix-hash-rollout-safety` with proposed toggles and migration steps.
maria: for immediate follow-ups:
- ajay: continue 1:1 monitoring for 30m and collect traces for any remaining stalls.
- julien & kevin: prepare diffs for canary dual-write implementation.
- lia & product-ops: customer comms and SLA hit calc.
- sara: schedule rollback postmortem and link to change.

ajay: I'm on watch. If any regression reappears, page me immediately. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks team — keep thread updated with metrics snippets and evidence for postmortem.

(Reaction summary: many :thumbsup: and :eyes: in-channel)

logs snippet:
```
2026-07-04T18:00:02Z cache_agent[streaming] WARN prefix_miss key=0x9a3f... version=3
2026-07-04T18:03:12Z deployer INFO env update PREFIX_HASH_VERSION=2
2026-07-04T18:05:13Z cache_agent INFO prefix_hit_rate=0.72 region=us-east-1
```

metrics query used:
```
SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) as p95, percentile(latency_ms,99) as p99 FROM streaming_requests
WHERE service IN ('chat-stream','completion-stream') AND time > now() - 1h
GROUP BY time(1m)
```

closing note: we'll create INC-2026-1845 postmortem draft and link here."
